canonical_title: Cues and data for targeted sensing system
subject_group: 10.1.5 Aerial refueling sensing, data, visual cues, and lighting systems compatibility

versions.title_at_revision: Cues and data for targeted sensing system
versions.text:
Standard: Cues and data (visual or equivalent) are provided on the air vehicle and can be received and interpreted by the targeted air vehicle sensing system and do not degrade targeted sensing system performance, under mission-defined environmental conditions to facilitate AR. Mission-defined environmental conditions include day, night, dusk, twilight, high and low sun angles, sun in and out of FOV, with and without NVIS, ambient moonlight (waxing and waning) in and out of FOV, diverse backgrounds (e.g., snow, ocean, desert, populated city lights, foliage dominant), above clouds, below clouds, and in clouds. a. Boom Tanker. Cues (visual or equivalent) for cleared to contact, position keeping, and breakaway are provided by the boom tanker can be received by the targeted receptacle equipped-receiver air vehicle. For current AR operations, these include receiver positioning markings, AR boom markings showing inner and outer receiver contact limit, size and movement indicators and associated lighting, exterior lighting, including flood lights, wing illumination, underbody illumination, boom nozzle illumination, PDLs, boom marker lights, position lights, rendezvous lights, formation lights, and any other exterior lighting necessary to accomplish AR activities. b. Drogue Tanker. Cues (visual or equivalent) for ready for contact, fuel system status, position keeping, and breakaway are provided by the drogue tanker can be received by the targeted probe-equipped receiver air vehicle. For current AR operations, these include receiver positioning markings, AR hose markings (including length intervals, inner and outer fuel transfer range and full trail exceedance), exterior lighting including flood lights, wing illumination, underbody illumination, wing pod illumination, engine nacelle illumination, drogue illumination, hose exit tunnel illumination, hose illumination, drogue system status lights, position lights, rendezvous lights, formation lights, and any other exterior lighting necessary to accomplish AR activities. c. Receptacle Receiver. Cues (visual or equivalent) needed to enable AR including receptacle system status and location are provided by the receiver and can be received by the targeted boom tanker air vehicle. For current AR operations these include boom lead-in markings in front of the receptacle, receptacle illumination, slipway illumination, position lights, rendezvous lights, formation lights, and any other exterior lighting necessary to accomplish AR activities. d. Probe Receiver. Cues (visual or equivalent) needed to enable AR including probe system status and location are provided by the receiver and can be received by the targeted drogue tanker air vehicle. For current AR operations these include probe illumination, position lights, rendezvous lights, formation lights, and any other exterior lighting necessary to accomplish AR activities. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of system specifications verifies necessary cues and data are provided for AR operations within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions. Examination of sensing system design verifies necessary cues and data to conduct AR operations are provided. Analysis.
  (1) Task analysis determines visual cues needed by targeted human viewed systems to accomplish AR. Analysis of air vehicle design verifies required data and visual cues are provided within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions.
  (2) For unmanned systems, computer modeling of refueling tasks determines data and associated performance parameters required for targeted unmanned systems to accomplish AR. Analysis of air vehicle design verifies data is provided. Demonstration.
    (1) Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies data and cues needed to conduct AR operations with targeted air vehicles are provided in simulated mission defined environmental conditions. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Hardware-in-the-loop laboratory testing verifies cues and data (visual and equivalent) needed to conduct AR is provided in simulated mission defined environmental conditions is provided. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
      (2) Flight test: Flight testing with targeted air vehicles verifies data and visual cues needed to accomplish AR within the system’s mission defined environmental conditions are provided and interpretable. Test points include various ambient lighting conditions (e.g., day, night, dusk), receiver join up, astern/pre-contact, contact position, multiple receivers, in contact maneuvering. A qualitative crewmember assessment will be used to verify data and visual cues for human operated systems.
